key_insight: In RL with verifiable rewards, momentum helps when the EMA coefficient is chosen large enough to stay in a safe regime that avoids overshoot, especially as sampling noise dominates at smaller learning rates.
engineering_relevance: For practical LLM post-training, tuning momentum upward can preserve a real optimization gain and improve validation accuracy without changing the core training setup.
method: Bandit model of RLVR with bias-corrected EMA momentum
Theoretical analysis of exact policy gradients vs sampled-gradient noise
Guideline: increase β as learning rate η decreases to keep η/(1−β) in the safe range
evidence_signal: Bandit simulations and RLVR experiments on Qwen3-4B-Base and Qwen2.5-32B validate the theory, with larger β1 improving mean validation accuracy by nearly 2 percentage points on the larger model.
watch_item: The benefit depends on staying below the overshoot threshold; overly aggressive momentum settings can destabilize training or lose gains under noisy gradient estimates.
paper_title: When Does Momentum Help in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards?
